To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AC field induced dynamic localization of minibands in coupled superlattices is characterized by the presence of two different regimes separated by a transition region.
the dynamics of a miniband system in an AC field is characterized by two different localization regimes, separated by a breakdown regime where the system is in a metallic phase.
the AC-field-induced breakdown of dynamic localization can be described as a field-induced insulator-metal like-transition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics and the control of electronic systems in the presence of a periodic potential.
the investigation of the electronic properties of low dimensional structures, with particular emphasis on the interplay between electron-electron and electron-phonon interaction.
the study of electronic states in low-dimensional semiconductor heterostructures, and in particular with the investigation of the effects of an external AC field on the minibands of superlattices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamic localization is not a single well-defined phenomenon but rather a complex one, which can be characterized in terms of different localization regimes, each of which is characterized by a different set of signatures.

a field induced insulating-metal transition can be identified in the system, by the observation of a suppression of a Peirles-like instability in a dynamic localization map, in a wide range of field frequencies, from low to high frequency limits.
the AC field induced suppression of the instability is a signature of a field induced metal-insulator transition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamic localization is an intrinsic phenomenon that is not limited by the perturbative approach.
the dynamic localization regime in the high frequency limit, is a consequence of the fact that the AC field cannot couple the miniband states to the continuum.
the dynamic localization regime is a very rich one, with many different regimes and signatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic localization is a robust effect, and that its signature can be detected in experiments by measuring a quasi-energy map as a function of field frequency and intensity.
the dynamic localization is a very sensitive function of the field frequency and intensity, with signatures of a field-induced insulator-metal like phase transition.
a dynamical localization can be tuned by the AC field intensity and frequency, thus opening a route towards the design of novel devices based on the control of dynamic localization.
